name: Mortenson
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Mortenson is the only US contractor at scale that holds both a hyperscale data-center building franchise and a fleet-scale renewable-power EPC franchise — and the AI buildout is fusing the two into one product. The family-owned Minneapolis builder jumped 12 spots to #10 on ENR's 2026 Top 400 on $10.85B of 2025 revenue (up from $4.9B in 2023 — more than doubling in two years), with ENR data showing ~45% of revenue in data centers and ~33% in power. It claims 11 GW of data centers delivered or underway, 47.8+ GW of wind, 17+ GW of solar, and 45,000+ MWh of storage, and it self-performs the gigawatt-class substations and medium-voltage distribution that pure building GCs must subcontract — visible at Lancium's Abilene AI campus (1 GW, 345 kV greenfield substation, all five main transformers energized by March 2026) and on Meta's Richland Parish campus, where Mortenson holds the sitework, MV-power, substation, water, and fiber scopes alongside Turner and DPR. Meta concentration is now the defining exposure: Richland Parish LA (~$50B deepened regional commitment), Lebanon IN (>$10B, 1 GW, co-delivered with Turner), and Beaver Dam WI ($1B) are all live Mortenson engagements. Collection gap: the company is 100% private and discloses no profitability, backlog, or balance-sheet data; revenue figures are self-reported ENR survey data.
ecosystemRole: Power-and-shell contractor to the AI buildout: top-10 US general contractor and historical #1 US wind builder that delivers hyperscale data-center campuses together with their substations, medium-voltage distribution, and onsite renewable/storage generation — the integration layer between the building and the grid that most building GCs cannot self-perform.

productsAndServices.name: Data Center Construction & Turnkey Campus Delivery
productsAndServices.description: Full-scope data-center delivery: site selection and land preparation, core-and-shell and fit-out construction, commissioning, power-distribution and substation EPC, prefabricated components via the BLUvera affiliate, master planning, and supply-chain management. Company claims 11 GW completed or under construction, 1,000+ dedicated data-center staff, and 20+ years in mission-critical work.
highlights: Meta Richland Parish, LA — one of three GCs (with Turner and DPR) on Meta's largest data center ($10B initial, ~4M sq ft; Meta deepened the regional commitment to ~$50B in July 2026); Mortenson scope: site prep/grading, underground utilities, MV distribution and substations, water/wastewater treatment, fiber; 7,500+ craft workers at peak (company figure)
Meta Lebanon, IN — co-delivering Meta's >$10B, ~4M sq ft, 1 GW second Indiana campus with Turner and Faith Technologies; first phase online early 2028
Meta Beaver Dam, WI — sole GC on the $1B, 700,000 sq ft dry-cooled facility (Meta's 30th globally), completion expected 2027

Lancium Abilene, TX — power-delivery EPC on one of the world's largest AI data-center buildouts: Phase 1 200 MW with 138 kV substation (2022-24); Phase 2 a 12.5-acre, 1 GW, 345 kV greenfield substation — first transformer energized 2025-12-19, all five main transformers by 2026-03-10
Other fleet: Eagle Mountain UT, DeKalb IL, three confidential Midwest campuses, Stream colocation work
productsAndServices.positioning: Alongside Turner and DPR on the largest Meta campuses rather than subordinate to them — differentiated by self-performed power scope (substations to 345 kV/1 GW class) that Turner, Holder, HITT, and DPR largely subcontract. Independent analysis pegs Mortenson's data-center revenue at an estimated $2-3B/yr and calls it a top-three GC in the space, concentrated in the Midwest/Mountain West (analyst estimate, not company-confirmed).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct negotiated contracts and framework relationships with hyperscalers and data-center developers; repeat-client model
productsAndServices.roadmap: Deepening Meta program execution through 2028 (Richland Parish phases, Lebanon IN first phase early 2028, Beaver Dam 2027); Hermantown MN ~700 MW Google-anchored campus in re-entitlement with an updated environmental review (~7 months from March 2026)

productsAndServices.name: Renewable Energy EPC (Wind, Solar, Storage)
productsAndServices.description: Self-perform EPC across the three utility-scale renewable classes: 47.8+ GW of wind across 290+ projects over 30+ years (historical #1 US wind builder), 17+ GW of solar across 120+ projects in 19 states, and 45,000+ MWh of battery storage across 60 projects in 11 years (all company figures). Battery-vendor experience spans Tesla, Samsung, BYD, LG, Fluence, Powin, and Wärtsilä.
highlights: Edwards & Sanborn (Terra-Gen), Kern County CA — largest US solar+storage at its early-2024 completion: 875 MWdc solar, 3,287 MWh storage, 1,300 MW interconnection, 1.9M+ First Solar modules; full EPC on both scopes with 1M+ injury-free hours
Nova Power Bank (Calpine), Menifee CA — 680 MW / 2,720 MWh standalone BESS on a demolished gas-plant site; fully complete June 2025

Darden Clean Energy (Intersect Power), Fresno County CA — full EPC on a ~1,500 MWdc solar + 4,600 MWh storage project (world's largest BESS when built, per the California Energy Commission); first project approved under California's AB 205 fast-track, completion targeted 2028

By 2010 Mortenson had installed 24% of all then-existing US wind capacity; ENR #2 in wind and #1 in energy storage today (company-cited ranks); Solar Power World #7 (2026) with ~2 GW installed in 2025
productsAndServices.positioning: Post-consolidation renewables peer set is Blattner (Quanta), Primoris, IEA (MasTec), SOLV, Sterling & Wilson — none of which hold a hyperscale building franchise. Building-GC rivals hold no comparable power franchise. The combination is Mortenson's structural differentiator.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC and BOP contracts with utilities, IPPs, and clean-energy developers; strong OEM turbine relationships; repowering programs
productsAndServices.roadmap: Darden through 2028; storage pipeline compounding on the #1 ENR storage rank; wind repowering as the installed-fleet ages

productsAndServices.name: Power Delivery, Substations & Grid Controls
productsAndServices.description: Self-performed high-voltage transmission, substation EPC to the 345 kV / 1 GW class, medium-voltage distribution, and underground utilities — sold both standalone and as the power layer of data-center campuses. The April 2026 acquisition of Nor-Cal Controls adds open-architecture SCADA/EMS engineering for solar, BESS, and microgrids, extending the franchise into grid-interface software and controls.
highlights: Abilene 1 GW / 345 kV greenfield substation for Lancium delivered in ~12 months from start to full energization (first transformer nine months in)
Richland Parish MV distribution and substation scope on Meta's largest campus
Nor-Cal Controls (acquired 2026-04-08, terms undisclosed): SCADA/EMS for solar, storage, and microgrids
Green hydrogen, EV/microgrid, and structured-cabling practices round out the energy-infrastructure stack
productsAndServices.positioning: The scope that turns a building GC into a power-and-shell integrator; competes with specialty T&D firms (Quanta, MasTec) inside a building-GC wrapper they lack
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC contracts within campus programs and standalone power-delivery awards
productsAndServices.roadmap: Integrating Nor-Cal Controls; scaling substation EPC with the AI-campus pipeline

productsAndServices.name: BLUvera Offsite Manufacturing (Industrialized Construction)
productsAndServices.description: Mortenson's manufacturing affiliate, born from schedule pressure on the hyperscale Eagle Mountain UT job: precast data-center elements installed 'like Lego blocks,' including modular 20-ft, 17,000-lb precast duct-bank sections, steel-frame wall panels, and hot-aisle containment, produced in mobile factories deployed adjacent to sites (e.g., DeKalb IL).

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess Mortenson is the only US contractor at scale holding both a hyperscale data-center building franchise and a fleet-scale power-EPC franchise, and that this pairing — not building volume alone — explains its 12-spot jump to ENR #10. Renewables rivals (Blattner/Quanta, MasTec, Primoris, SOLV) lack a hyperscale building book; building rivals (Turner, Holder, HITT, DPR) subcontract most gigawatt-class power scope. The Abilene 1 GW/345 kV substation and the Richland Parish power scopes are the direct evidence.

2. (High confidence) We assess Meta concentration is Mortenson's defining commercial exposure through at least 2028: three simultaneous engagements (Richland Parish LA within a ~$50B deepened regional commitment, Lebanon IN >$10B co-prime, Beaver Dam WI $1B solo) almost certainly account for a large share of the $13.85B of 2025 new contracts. A Meta capex pause would hit Mortenson harder than any peer except possibly Turner.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess the storage franchise is becoming Mortenson's second growth engine after data centers: three consecutive record-scale BESS projects (Edwards & Sanborn 3,287 MWh, Nova 2,720 MWh, Darden 4,600 MWh) plus the company-cited ENR #1 storage rank position it to capture the AI-driven firming-capacity cycle, and the Nor-Cal Controls acquisition signals intent to own the grid-interface controls layer rather than rent it.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the development arm (Mortenson Properties) is being repositioned from family real-estate portfolio to data-center origination channel — Hermantown (~700 MW, Google revealed as end user) is the test case. If the re-entitlement survives, Mortenson gains a deal-flow channel no building-GC peer has; if it fails, expect the model to shift toward pre-permitted land partnerships. The MCEA litigation makes this the highest-variance item in the book.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess private, third-generation family ownership is a net execution advantage in this cycle: no earnings pressure to chase margin over risk discipline, patient capital for BLUvera factories and the Nor-Cal acquisition, and an orderly 2025 CEO succession. The cost is opacity — no profitability, backlog, or balance-sheet disclosure — which is itself a collection gap we cannot close from public sources.

6. (Low confidence) We assess Mortenson's data-center revenue at roughly $2-3B/yr based on a single independent analysis of ENR mix data; the company does not confirm segment revenue. Treat sector-level precision here as indicative only.
